title: Chronic Ear Infections? Discover How an ENT Doctor Can Help
htmlContent:
Viruses or bacteria can cause ear infections. Your middle ear can be the most vulnerable. You can experience tremendous pain due to fluid accumulation or recurrence behind the eardrum. It can be diagnosed as acute otitis media (AOM) if the fluid gathers under the eardrum. However, if it stays there for a long time or recurs, you can suffer from chronic otitis media with effusion. Due to this, you can face hearing problems and other ear infections. Some suffer from an other chronic condition called chronic suppurative otitis media. They have to deal with continuous or recurring ear discharge. This ear infection can be linked with acute otitis media and perforated eardrums developed in childhood. Please don't ignore chronic ear infections, which can escalate into several complications. Due to continuous inflammation, one can fall victim to a unique condition called mastoiditis that causes swelling or redness with AOM symptoms behind the ear. Or, they can take the form of a specific type of skin cell growth in the middle ear. It's referred to as cholesteatoma. So, seek help from an ear nose throat specialist if you suspect any symptoms or discomfort in your ear. They can suggest the best remedy or treatment.
  • Chronic ear infection symptoms
These infections may not have immediately recognizable patterns or signs. However, you can experience hearing problems due to long-term fluid buildup. If you take more time to comprehend speech, struggle to read or speak, have balance issues, short attention spans, etc., you must visit your ENT. Chronic infections can also occur due to otitis media with effusion, which usually affects kids. The condition occurs after an ear infection clears up, but the fluid sticks in the middle ear.
  • Chronic ear infection treatment
After investigating your ear thoroughly and listening to your symptoms, your ENT can suggest a few treatments. Some clean the earwax and fluid to speed up healing. You can be recommended fever and pain relief medications. If it’s a bacterial infection, you can be prescribed antibiotics. Anyone with a hole or damaged eardrum can be given antibiotic ear drops. Antifungal ear drops or other such solutions can be advised for fungal infections. Different individuals can be suggested different treatment procedures due to their specific conditions. Ensure you consult a trusted ENT in your city. It will eliminate most of your worries.
  • Risks associated with not treating chronic ear infections
Chronic infections often result from persistent acute ear infections. As prevention, you must seek help with acute infections, which usually clog the eustachian tube, spanning the middle ear and the back of the throat. Kids are more vulnerable to this infection as their tubes tend to be short and narrow. Nevertheless, the fluid accumulation can trigger an infection, leading to pain and other challenges. Whether caused by bacteria, the common cold, or something else, untreated chronic ear infections can interfere with the upper respiratory tract. Some chronic ear infections can heal by themselves. However, if you don't feel improvement after three days or the symptoms persist, fix an appointment with your ENT. Timely checkups and treatment can accelerate recovery and reduce discomfort.
